statement: You receive a sorted row of integers and a target integer. Print two numbers separated by a space: the index of the first occurrence of the target and the index of the last occurrence. If the target is absent, print -1 -1. Two binary searches solve it; one search that stops on any equality does not.
constraints: The row is sorted ascending and may contain duplicates.

example.why: The 8s occupy indices 3 and 4; the first search hunts left, the second hunts right.

hint: Run the remembered-answer loop twice: once continuing left after a hit, once continuing right.
mistake: Walking linearly outward from one found index - a row of all target values turns that walk into n steps.
